analysis.title: The Case for Small Caps (Economic Note, November 2025)
key_insights: Silvercrest argues small caps are trading below their own long-term average valuation on trailing 12-month P/E, while large caps look expensive versus their own history.
Valuation comparison uses the Russell 1000 against the S&P SmallCap 600, chosen because it has higher quality than the Russell 2000 and avoids noise from unprofitable companies.
Small caps hit a turning point in the late 1990s after a ten-year, -7% annualized lag versus large caps. Furey Research Partners show similar inflections in the 1930s and 1950s.
The early phase of a turnaround is usually led by speculative corners via short covering. Heavily shorted stocks have rallied in recent weeks, dragging unprofitable names higher.

For the rally to be sustainable, leadership must broaden to durable, earnings-driven names. The rally is eight months old as of November 2025, within the window when quality leadership has historically emerged.
Small companies are increasingly using AI, which could lift productivity, margins and earnings. Investor attention is starting to scrutinize valuations of large AI infrastructure builders.

Small caps offer liquidity, transparency and a contrarian timing profile versus private investments, which are illiquid, variably transparent and momentum-driven. The note says investors need not choose between the two.
Diversification case: from March 2000 to September 2002 the S&P 600 fell -8.4% versus -43.9% for the Russell 1000. At a 10% weight that is 355 bps of added portfolio return.
Small caps skew more to Health Care and Industrials and have a more domestically focused revenue base.
Three catalysts: domestic-focused legislation and the mid-term cycle, rising M&A with private equity dry powder, and a falling rate backdrop expected over the next 18 months.
Smaller firms carry more floating-rate bank debt, so lower rates disproportionately ease financing stress and raise investor interest.
Recent small-cap rallies have been short-lived or driven by low-quality, retail momentum names. Citadel Securities tracks activity in lower-priced shares.

Selection criteria: under-covered success stories (fewer than six analysts per Russell 2000 company vs about 30 for large caps), situational quality with strong balance sheets, and aligned management with an execution record. Active selection is favored.

sector_views.rationale: Cheap versus own history, multiple catalysts including rates, M&A and domestic spending, and diversification away from large-cap tech.
Small caps offer greater exposure to these sectors than large caps, adding fundamental diversification.
Large caps look expensive versus history and the current tech cycle will eventually end, so adding small caps now diversifies.

earnings_insights: No specific EPS or revenue figures are cited. The note expects earnings growth to broaden toward small caps as AI adoption lifts margins.

macro_indicators.reading: Extended cycle of rate declines likely over the next 18 months
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower rates ease financing stress for small caps with floating-rate debt and typically boost interest in economically sensitive smaller companies.

trade_ideas.description: Increase small-cap exposure using active stock selection in the Russell 2000 and S&P 600 universe
trade_ideas.rationale: Small caps are cheap versus history, catalysts are emerging, and the exposure diversifies concentrated large-cap tech risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Rallies have been short-lived or driven by lower-quality speculative names.

risk_factors: The current rally could stall if it stays led by speculative, unprofitable and heavily shorted stocks.
Small-cap quality is uneven within the Russell 2000.
Large-cap tech cycle may not end soon, delaying relative gains.
Past small-cap rallies have been short-lived.
Rate cuts may not materialize as expected.
charts_described: Fig. 3 plots the trailing 10-year annualized return of the Russell 2000 minus the Russell 1000, with the late-1990s turning point at about -7% annualized per the text.
Fig. 4 plots the Russell 1000, Russell 2000 and S&P 600 normalized as of 1/2/1996, showing small caps held up better in the 1999-2000 cycle shift per the text.
vol_and_positioning: Heavily shorted stocks have rallied in recent weeks, consistent with short covering in the first phase of a small-cap turnaround.
Citadel Securities tracks activity in lower-priced shares, which is driven by retail investors and momentum.
Allocator flows have favored large caps and private equity over the past ten years.

tension_points.bull_case: Small caps are cheap versus their own history, a turnaround phase is under way, and catalysts include lower rates, M&A and domestic spending, with AI adoption lifting margins.
tension_points.bear_case: Recent rallies were short-lived or driven by low-quality, heavily shorted and retail momentum names, and Russell 2000 quality is uneven.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Leadership failing to extend from speculative corners to durable, earnings-driven small caps.

theme_stances.key_argument: Investors do not need to choose, and small caps add liquidity, transparency and contrarian timing.
